description: OS-neutral lock port. Callers (Node facade, Rust crate, hook) see only these operations; the fd or job handling lives in the driver.

fields.name: registry lock name (packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json)
fields.path: absolute path of the lock file, created once and never removed while the resource lives
fields.predecessorKinds: optional nonempty string[]: reject other recorded kinds under the kernel lock before ordinary predecessor cleanup

fileRules: opened O_RDWR (NFSv4 and BSD refuse an exclusive lock on a read-only fd)
the description is always FD_CLOEXEC except inside exactly one spawn that borrows it, through an explicit fd mapping
after acquire, fstat(fd).ino must equal stat(path).ino; otherwise close and retry
release and borrower close only; nobody calls LOCK_UN on any copy of a description
windowsFileRules: the lock is LockFileEx on the process's own handle, offset 0, length 1; an ERROR_IO_PENDING answer is an error, never a held lock
the lock belongs to the locking process and is never carried by an inheritable or duplicated handle: a child holding a handle does not hold the lock
every successful lock is unlocked explicitly (UnlockFileEx) before its handle closes; the close-only rule above applies to POSIX descriptions, which borrowed copies share
after acquire the locked handle and a fresh handle to the path must name the same file (volume serial plus the 128-bit file id, FileIdInfo); otherwise unlock, close and retry
a path on a remote volume (GetDriveTypeW == DRIVE_REMOTE, or FileRemoteProtocolInfo readable) is refused with unavailable/unsupported-filesystem and guarantee exclusion none

killWaitMs.meaning: upper bound on waiting for a predecessor domain that was already killed to be signaled; never a wait-for-drain

acquire.rule: returns acquired only when BOTH hold: the kernel lock is held AND the predecessor domain recorded next to the lock file is empty (predecessor.v1.json). A free kernel lock alone is not proof.

clear_domain.rule: While holding exclusion, observe the holder domain empty without killing, then remove only its unchanged predecessor record. Unknown or live domains and replaced resources refuse. Node handle.clearDomain() uses the inherited description or existing lock-hold request channel.

release.rule: the holder releases only after its own domain is empty (run_borrowed already waited for the child, killed leftovers and waited for empty). Release closes every copy it owns, then (for exclusive Linux handles) uses positive kernel lock-table evidence and an inode-checked, noncreating shared try-lock probe to prove no copy of its description still holds the lock (a short table read is not EOF); a blocked or uncertain probe enters the full tagged scan, killing escaped holders of it (direct children waited, copies of this process's live handles spared); unresolved within the bounded wait returns lock-release-stuck. Drop uses the same settle; shared handles close directly. The brief shared probe may make a concurrent exclusive Try acquirer report held; no copy of the original description is retained.

run_borrowed.rule: the only way a child command passes with the holder's authority. POSIX: hands the description to exactly one child through an explicit fd mapping (default slot 3, env FGOS_LOCK_FD=<name>:3). Windows: runs the child inside a named kill-on-close job the locking process creates, with env FGOS_LOCK_JOB=<lock name>:<job name>; no handle is passed. When argv[0] is git, the call prepends -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false. After the child exits: kill what is left in the domain, wait for the domain to be empty, only then return. Node fd borrows and native loans carry live async sibling roots into the same Rust drain; siblings are waited on/fail closed, never signalled. Starting a borrow or minting a native loan while a drain snapshot is active refuses before spawn with retryable borrow-drain-in-progress.

input.handle: opaque EX handle returned by acquire
input.spec: BorrowSpec: argv, cwd, env, clear_env; stdio superseded by explicit I/O

run_borrowed_io.rule: Extended 2026-10-18 for Git Publication: run_borrowed with explicit input, bounded capture and deadline; same lifecycle as run_borrowed. Synchronous scoped lifecycle: no child, pipe or lock description escapes. Unix uses the same explicit fd mapping, preparation, predecessor handling and leftover cleanup as run_borrowed. Output overflow or deadline kills the child, waits without reaping, drains the existing borrow domain and reaps before returning the named refusal. Cleanup failure takes precedence as borrow-leftover-not-killed, as for run_borrowed. No new containment guarantee or admission barrier.

platforms.windows: borrow-io-unsupported before spawn; existing run_borrowed behavior unchanged

borrowerCheck.posix: fd 3 has the same dev:ino as the lock file and a non-blocking exclusive lock on it succeeds (lock-fd --borrowed-check)

windows.env: FGOS_LOCK_JOB=<lock name>:<job name>; no slot is read
passesOnlyWhenAll: (a) the env names this lock and a job
(b) the predecessor record names that job and a holder tuple
(d) the recorded holder (pid + creation time) is in this process's ancestor chain and probe sees the lock held

meaning.job-missing: (a) fails: env absent, malformed, or naming another lock
meaning.record-mismatch: (b) fails: record absent, unreadable, or naming another job or no holder tuple
meaning.holder-not-ancestor: (d) fails: the recorded holder is not an ancestor
meaning.lock-not-held: (d) fails: probe sees the lock free

windows.secrecy: the job name is not a secret: it is written in the record and the env. The authority comes from (c) and (d).

probe.rule: non-blocking LOCK_SH attempt that never obstructs another holder; the shared lock is dropped at once.

holders.notes: Linux scans /proc/*/fdinfo/* for a lock: line on the inode of the lock file. macOS and Windows report unlistable (Win32 has no API that lists byte-range lock holders).

input.path: directory the lock files live in

held.domain: present only for predecessor-domain-not-empty: the predecessor domain record (predecessor.v1.json)

errors.lock-release-stuck: release could not prove the original description released or end its holders/helper within the bounded wait; reports leftoversKilled and remaining pids; the lock may still be held
errors.borrow-busy: run_borrowed was called while another borrow of the same handle is still running, or release was called during a borrow

invariants: timeout and held never leave a description open: the lock is released before the result is returned
predecessor-domain-not-empty is returned after the lock was released again
no result infers ownership or liveness from a pid, a TTL or an mtime; Linux release compares the kernel locker stamp only to this live process

levelMeaning.kernel: enforced by the kernel and measured on a real machine
levelMeaning.kernel-unmeasured: kernel semantics expected, no measurement yet
levelMeaning.job-scoped: enforced through a job plus the predecessor rule; the borrow level of the Windows driver (not an exclusion level)
levelMeaning.unsupported: the driver does not provide it; the caller must not rely on it
levelMeaning.none: no guarantee (network filesystem); the driver refuses the lock with a named error

guarantee.containment: macOS holder-lock containment is best-effort and is reported in notes, not in a level

probe-holder.meaning: takes the lock on P in its own process and reports, used by the two-process semantics probe

job-keeper.meaning: second owner of a borrow job, outside it; exits only when the holder finished (or its handle is signaled) and the job view is empty (predecessor.v1.json keeperExit)

helperRoles.status: internal: no CLI promise, argv may change with the crate
helperRoles.helperExe: the crate API takes the helper executable as an explicit HelperExe path parameter; production passes the current executable, tests of the binary crates pass their own binary
